reasoning: The evidence shows Trump won the 2024 election and took office in January 2025. Current inflation data from September 2025 shows rates of 2.9-3.4%, above the 2.5% threshold. Key findings: (1) Inflation fell from 3.0% in January to 2.3% in April but rebounded to 2.9% in August; (2) Core inflation reached 3.1% in August, highest since January; (3) Tariffs are contributing approximately 2.3% to inflation; (4) Goldman Sachs projects tariff pass-through to consumers will rise from 22% to 67%; (5) Multiple sources indicate inflation is reaccelerating, not declining. While one source claims inflation has decreased since January, most evidence contradicts this, showing recent acceleration. With 9 months remaining in 2025 and current inflation above 2.5% with upward pressure from tariffs, achieving sub-2.5% inflation appears unlikely.
